title: Make binding inputs fail fast and declare the mesh/material contract
description:
## Summary
The skinned-mesh binding stack is mathematically solid but under-specified at its edges. Four P2 findings from the 2026-09-12 audits share one mechanism: the binding layer silently substitutes defaults for present-but-invalid inputs and silently drops mesh/material payload it does not declare. Residual lineage: TSK-0132 (Done).

## Scope
- SK-01/SK-02: `ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring.ResolveBoneRadius` silently substitutes `policy.FallbackBoneRadius` for a present-but-non-finite/non-positive radius. Split the production path (reject invalid, require morphology) from a clearly named synthetic-test helper.
- SK-05: `WeightFor` does not share `Author`'s validation; either centralize or document it as a caller-validated primitive.
- SK-07/SK-08: `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer.BuildSkinningMeshCopy` preserves only normals, tangents, uv, uv2, uv3, colors, submesh triangles, bindposes, weights; `Bind` fills missing materials with `null` instead of failing. Declare and validate the supported mesh/material contract, or preserve the full payload.
- Out of scope: influence-domain locality policy itself (TSK-0147, InProgress) and animated bounds/culling (TSK-0200).

## Acceptance Criteria
- A supplied-but-invalid bone radius is rejected (or explicitly reported) on the production path; a missing radius may still use the documented default.
- A synthetic/test-only influence builder exists with a name that cannot be mistaken for production.
- `WeightFor` and `Author` cannot disagree about validity; one implementation owns the rule.
- The supported mesh-channel and material-cardinality contract is written down and enforced or asserted; unsupported input is rejected or reported, not silently degraded.
- Focused EditMode/Runtime tests cover each of the four rules, and each test names the historical failure mechanism it targets.

## Validation
- Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runtime/CreatureSkinnedMeshRendererTests.cs extended (mesh copy + material cardinality + invalid radius rejection).
- New or extended weight-authoring tests for `WeightFor`/`Author` parity.
- Full-solution compile before the focused test run.

## Findings
- Verified in current source: `ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring.ResolveBoneRadius` returns `policy.FallbackBoneRadius` when `supplied` fails `> 0f && IsFinite`.
- Verified in current source: `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer.BuildSkinningMeshCopy` copies only uv/uv2/uv3 (not uv4+) and `Bind` writes `null` for missing materials without failing.
- Audit note: the deep-dive report lists "UV0-UV2" while the deformation audit lists "UV0-UV3"; current source copies uv, uv2, uv3. Treat the source as authoritative.

## Blockers
- None. This is source-verifiable; Unity is needed only for the renderer-level acceptance test.

## Next Step
Write the mesh/material contract as an explicit code comment plus assertion, then make the radius-resolution policy fail-fast and split the synthetic helper.
